Hi Daniel / Emily —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and what we heard from your infra/security teams:

- Primary goal: run inference for clinical NLP features inside Acme Health’s VPC or on-prem to meet data residency and PHI controls.
- Evaluation focus: network topology (control plane connectivity vs fully air-gapped), KMS/HSM integration, audit/logging, and an initial perf/cost baseline vs hyperscaler-managed endpoints.

What Redwood can offer (short):
- Private deployment options: hosted control plane with PrivateLink, or fully self-hosted control plane + inference nodes deployed in your VPC/on-prem.
- Air-gap feasibility: we do support an air-gapped on-prem deployment (no outbound internet required) but it requires a self-hosted control plane and a small offline install for initial model artifacts + updates.
- Differentiators vs hyperscalers: production-first runtime optimizations (batching, KV cache), predictable unit economics for steady-state inference, and first-class rollout/rollback/rollback metrics tailored to inference workloads.

Attachments: sharing two artifacts to help next steps — redwood-private-networking-overview.pdf (networking options + diagrams) and mvp-airgap-checklist.xlsx (what we need to validate for an air-gapped POC).

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical kickoff with your infra & CISO to validate network requirements and confirm control-plane preference (managed PrivateLink vs self-hosted). 60–90 min.
2) Run a short air-gap feasibility test: we provide a checklist and a small test image (no PHI) to validate full offline inference and access to KMS/HSM.
3) Baseline perf test: 1–2 models, 1000 sample requests, capture latency and cost.

Can we target next-week slots for the technical kickoff? I’m proposing Tue/Wed (3/3 or 3/4) morning PST — please share what works.

Thanks — I’ll loop Aditya for technical details and Vivek for pricing/contract boundary items.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Redwood private / VPC / air-gapped feasibility — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Daniel / Emily —

Quick answers ahead of the kickoff:

1) Control plane connectivity:
- Hosted control plane + PrivateLink: inference nodes communicate with the control plane over PrivateLink (no public internet egress required). Telemetry and metrics are proxied through PrivateLink endpoints; we do not require outbound 0.0.0.0/0.
- Self-hosted control plane: you run the control plane in your VPC or on-prem. No outbound connectivity required unless you choose to fetch model updates from Redwood. For a fully air-gapped setup, we recommend self-hosted control plane and manual model/artifact transfer.

2) KMS/HSM integration:
- We support customer-managed KMS via either: (a) Cloud KMS with a private connect (e.g., Cloud HSM in a VPC) or (b) On-prem HSM + internal KMS via our pluggable KMS connector. For option (b) we’ll run a lightweight connector inside your network that talks to your HSM over the internal fabric. Keys never leave your HSM.

3) Air-gap install footprint / model artifacts:
- Initial runtime: ~8–16 GB for our runtime and dependencies (containerized), plus model artifacts size which depends on model choice and quantization. For a small evaluator model (7B quantized to 4-bit), expect 10–20 GB of model files; for larger models scale up accordingly.
- We’ll provide a sizing worksheet in the kickoff and a sample disk image for the test.

Proposed POC test plan (high level):
- Network validation: confirm PrivateLink route table, security groups, and MTU.
- KMS validation: perform a sample encrypt/decrypt flow with a key on your HSM via the connector.
- Offline inference test: run a small batching workload with synthetic data to validate latency and cache behavior.

I’ve attached a short networking diagram and the MVP checklist to help your infra team.

Looking forward to Wed 3/4 10:00 PST — I and one of our infra engs (will be on the invite) will join.

--
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
